principles.statement: Context is assembled from the graph, not recalled from a summary — resolve links to their containers before reasoning about them.
principles.rationale: A summary of a summary loses the structure that makes the context accurate; the graph stores relationships precisely so they can be walked when needed.

principles.statement: Prefer the most recently verified source when two context sources disagree.
principles.rationale: Stale context silently contradicts fresh state; verification timestamps exist to arbitrate exactly this conflict.

principles.statement: Note which scope a piece of context came from — global, workspace, or project — before using it.
principles.rationale: A global policy and a project-local exception can both be true; conflating their scopes produces wrong conclusions.

heuristics.name: Relationship before content
heuristics.description: When evaluating a container, check what it links to and what links to it before trusting its standalone content.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Any container discovered by search rather than direct reference.
examples: A jurisdiction rule whose scope links to an EU baseline inherits constraints its text never mentions.

heuristics.name: Scope conflict check
heuristics.description: If two context items contradict, first check whether they differ in scope before treating it as a real contradiction.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Any apparent conflict between stored facts.
examples: 'Deploy on Friday' (project A) vs 'never deploy Fridays' (global) — scopes differ, not facts.

decision_rules.condition: Context was found by keyword match only, with no relationship walk.
decision_rules.action: Treat as a lead, not a fact — verify via container resolution or a related edge before citing it as grounding.
